title: A Parent Who Will Not Let Go
overview: God speaks like a hurt but loving parent, remembering how he raised Israel, warning of the disaster their turning away will bring, and then refusing to give them up.

parts.label: Called out of Egypt (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: God looks back on freeing Israel from slavery in Egypt as calling a beloved son, yet the more he called, the more they turned to Baal and other local Canaanite gods. Christians have also read verse 1 as pointing to Jesus, because Matthew's Gospel applies it to the child Jesus returning from Egypt.

parts.label: Taught to walk (vv. 3-4)
parts.note: Ephraim, the leading tribe of the north, stands for the whole northern kingdom of Israel, pictured as a toddler whose parent held its arms, healed it and fed it. The Hebrew of verse 4 can mean lifting a child to the cheek or easing the yoke off an ox's jaw so it can eat, and scholars are unsure which image is meant.

parts.label: What turning away brings (vv. 5-7)
parts.note: Israel had looked to Egypt for help against the rising empire of Assyria, but Assyria would end up ruling them, with war in their cities. This happened when Assyria conquered the northern kingdom around 722 BC, though verse 7 is hard to translate and versions differ.

parts.label: God's heart turns (vv. 8-9)
parts.note: Admah and Zeboiim were towns destroyed along with Sodom and Gomorrah, and God asks how he could ever do that to Israel. He says he will not act on his fierce anger, because he is God and not a human who strikes back in rage.

parts.label: Coming home (vv. 10-11)
parts.note: God's voice is pictured as a lion's roar calling his scattered children back from the west, from Egypt and from Assyria. They come trembling like small birds, and he settles them in their homes again.

parts.label: Lies and Judah (v. 12)
parts.note: Israel is accused of surrounding God with lies, but the Hebrew about Judah, the southern kingdom, is unclear, so some translations call Judah faithful and others call it unruly. In Hebrew Bibles this verse begins chapter 12.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether the promise of return in verses 10 and 11 was fulfilled when exiles came back long ago, still awaits a future regathering of the Jewish people, or is mainly fulfilled spiritually through Jesus.
think: When someone you have cared for keeps walking away, what makes it possible, or impossible, to keep loving them?
